haiku-low.q1: It becomes durable when the business transaction commits, as a pending row in notifications; it exists only if that commit succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers it again; a message not acknowledged within 30 seconds is delivered again. Delivery is at least once.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts total. Waits 1, 2, 4, then 8 minutes between attempts. After the fifth failure, the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update first, order_confirmed 3 days later, password_reset 3 days after that. Before it moves, service must show p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 seconds on order_confirmed.
haiku-low.q5: The notification id, the row's id, passed as idempotency_key. If MailRelay already accepted that key within 24 hours, it drops the repeat and reports success.
haiku-low.q6: A relay thread publishes service rows to notifications.requested every 5 seconds. The monolith is done once the broker confirms and published_at is set.
haiku-low.q7: enqueue_notification decides by reading the notify.route.<type> flag when the row is created; the route is set once and never changed.
haiku-low.q8: The deliveries table keys on notification id, so a second copy's insert does nothing. MailRelay also drops repeats sent with the same key.
haiku-low.q9: Only after the deliveries insert commits. If it crashes before acknowledging, the broker redelivers within 30 seconds and the insert does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's deliveries table. The sender's poll, every 5 seconds, takes due pending rows using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and updates attempts and next_attempt_at.
haiku-low.q11: They keep route service. The relay still publishes unpublished ones, and the service finishes them. Do not stop the service until its pending deliveries reach zero.
haiku-low.q12: Id, type, email, payload, and created_at travel on notifications.requested. The service renders the email from its own copy of the templates.

sonnet.q1: It becomes durable when business code's enqueue_notification inserts a pending row into the monolith's notifications table inside its own transaction. The row exists only if the business transaction commits.
sonnet.q2: The broker redelivers it if it is not acknowledged within 30 seconds (at-least-once delivery).
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts total. Waits after failures: 1 min after attempt 1, 2 min after 2, 4 min after 3, 8 min after 4. If attempt 5 fails, the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: First shipping_update, then order_confirmed 3 days later (no open problems), then password_reset 3 days after that. Each runs at least 3 days. Before password_reset moves, the service must show p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 seconds on order_confirmed over its 3-day run. Old worker removal comes 7 days after password_reset moves.
sonnet.q5: An idempotency_key, set to the notification id (the row id). If MailRelay already accepted that key in the last 24 hours, it drops the new send and reports success.
sonnet.q6: The relay thread in each monolith instance reads service rows with empty published_at every 5 seconds, publishes (id, type, email, payload, created_at) to notifications.requested, waits for broker confirmation, and sets published_at. NOT STATED for any single moment when the monolith considers its part done beyond that; the monolith row stays pending until the final result is copied back via notifications.result.
sonnet.q7: The route column on the notifications row, set by enqueue (business code's enqueue_notification) at row creation, based on the notify.route.<type> flag (service if on, monolith if off or flag read fails). It is set once and never changes.
sonnet.q8: The Store step inserts a deliveries row keyed by notification id; if a row with that id already exists it does nothing. Also MailRelay drops repeats of the same idempotency key (id) within 24 hours.
sonnet.q9: It acknowledges only after the deliveries insert commits (before any sending, which happens later by the poll). If it crashes before acknowledging, the broker redelivers within 30 seconds and the insert does nothing if the row already exists.
sonnet.q10: In the service's deliveries table (attempts, next_attempt_at, status). The sender's 5-second poll acts on it, taking pending rows whose next_attempt_at has passed and updating attempts and next_attempt_at per the retry schedule.
sonnet.q11: Nothing changes for them: rows keep their route (service). The relay still publishes unpublished service rows, the service still finishes them, and the old worker touches only monolith rows. Only new rows get route monolith. The service must not be stopped until its pending deliveries reach zero.
sonnet.q12: Id, type, email, payload, and created_at, published to notifications.requested. The email content is produced in the service: the sender renders the template using the service's own copy of the three templates.
